meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/02, Monday 3 June 2024). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: June 2024 series, despite the download folder's Nov 24 label — this paper is dated Monday 3 June 2024. J560/02 is one of OCR's two NON-calculator papers (the other is /05); OCR's paper 1 is a calculator paper, unlike both other boards. No per-question total is printed, so the whole-paper sum against the published 100 is the only check, and this file passes it.

coding_notes: mark_split is derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes rather than quoted; see OCR-JUN24-F-P1 for the reasoning. q26 is the ONE row left without a mark_split: the printed routes in the extracted mark scheme account for four of that part's five marks and the fifth could not be attributed, and a guessed split is worse than none.

q22b (circle the point most likely to be the pupil who left early) is an outlier-identification item, which a 2026-09-04 user ruling left untagged when the alternatives were range and mean. Here it is tagged scatter_graphs, because reading an anomalous point off a scatter diagram is inside that node's own territory rather than outside the taxonomy. Flagged in case that ruling should extend to this case too.
q5b (mark the complement on a probability scale) tagged mutually_exclusive_events, not calculating_simple_probability — the demand is that the two probabilities sum to 1.
q15b/c tagged converting_measurements first: the marks turn on litres-to-millilitres, and the division that follows is the arithmetic on top of it.
q21b (an assumption behind a journey-time answer) tagged compound_units, the skill the assumption is about — that the driver holds the speed limit throughout.
q27bii (the longer side, from the roots) tagged substitution: one follow-through mark for putting the positive root back into an expression.
